headline_marked: [[SSC pass rate hits 19-year low]] at 62.25%, nearly 7 lakh fail nationwide
headline: SSC pass rate hits 19-year low at 62.25%, nearly 7 lakh fail nationwide
summary: With 62.25% passing and 116,676 achieving GPA-5, students dissatisfied with their results can apply for re-evaluation through an online process.
details: The results for the 2026 SSC and equivalent examinations have been published, revealing a nationwide average pass rate of 62.25%. This marks a 19-year low, with a total of 116,676 students achieving a GPA-5 across the nine general education boards, madrasa, and technical education boards.
For students who did not achieve their expected results or failed in any subject, the education boards have introduced an opportunity for result re-evaluation, also known as a 'board challenge'.
The application fee for re-evaluation is BDT 150 per subject. For two-paper subjects like English or Bangla, applications must be submitted for both papers.
Fees can be paid through bKash, Nagad, and Sonali Seba. The application process is entirely online, with no manual or direct written applications accepted.

To apply, students must first visit the official re-evaluation website, rescrutiny.eduboardresults.gov.bd. They need to fill in their roll number, registration number, and select their education board from a drop-down menu before clicking 'submit'.

In the next step, an active mobile number must be provided, as the final re-evaluation results will be sent via SMS to this number. The student's subject-wise results will be displayed, allowing them to select the subjects for re-evaluation and proceed to payment.

The total fee amount will be shown on the screen, which can then be paid via bKash, Nagad, or Sonali Seba. After successful payment, the application is completed by clicking the 'submit' button on the portal.

Students can add additional subjects even after submitting the initial application, without needing to re-enter their mobile number. However, once fees are submitted, applied subjects cannot be changed or cancelled, and the paid amount is non-refundable.

headline_marked: [[Salman Shah's mother denies romantic link with Shabnur]] 30 years after actor's death
headline: Salman Shah's mother denies romantic link with Shabnur 30 years after actor's death
summary: After three decades, Neela Chowdhury states her son viewed Shabnur as a sister, echoing Shabnur's long-held stance against persistent rumors of a love affair.
details: Three decades after the untimely death of Dhallywood icon Salman Shah, his mother, Neela Chowdhury, has publicly stated that her son never had a romantic relationship with actress Shabnur. This statement comes amidst persistent rumors about their personal connection, which often overshadowed their celebrated on-screen pairing.

Shabnur herself has consistently maintained that her relationship with Salman Shah was akin to that of a brother and sister. She often mentioned that Salman, who had no sisters, affectionately called her 'Picchi' (little one) and that their families shared a close bond.

The topic resurfaced recently following the arrest of actor Don in connection with the Salman Shah murder case. During discussions about various aspects of her son's life, Neela Chowdhury addressed the nature of Salman's relationship with Shabnur.

Neela Chowdhury emphasized that Salman viewed Shabnur as a sister and was supportive of her, seeing her as someone dependent on him. She clarified that while there was a deep affection, it was not the love of a romantic partner but rather the love one shares with a dear family member.

However, Neela Chowdhury also alleged that Shabnur had previously tried to imply a romantic connection, and these reports were later sensationalized. Despite this, she firmly reiterated that a romantic relationship never existed between them.

Shabnur, in her own statements to Prothom Alo, has always denied any romantic involvement, asserting she respected Salman as a brother. She expressed frustration that some individuals and journalists exploited their professional relationship for personal gain and sensational stories after Salman's death.

Salman Shah debuted in 1993 with 'Keyamat Theke Keyamat' and later formed a highly popular on-screen duo with Shabnur, starting with 'Tumi Amar'. In his short four-year career, Salman starred in 27 films, 14 of which were with Shabnur, with most achieving commercial success.

Shabnur fondly recalled their excellent on-screen chemistry and off-screen friendship, describing Salman as a big-hearted, humble, and dedicated artist. She also highlighted her close friendship with Salman's wife, Samira, and the strong family ties that developed between them, often involving joint outings and dinners during shoots.

Salman Shah passed away on September 6, 1996, in Dhaka. Despite the passage of time, discussions surrounding his death, personal life, and relationships with co-stars continue to captivate public interest.
